title: Kernel-aware prefill prefetch + queueing heuristics to reduce prompt preprocessing overhead
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background: Prefill-side overhead for short interactive prompts remains a dominant contributor to p95/p99 latency on our hosted API for many customers. Even when decode kernels are optimized, the end-to-end request often suffers from: (1) serial UTF-8/token scanning and normalization cost, (2) prefill tokenization and KV prewarm that runs on the same CPU cores used by scheduling decisions, and (3) suboptimal kernel selection / queueing where microbatches are dispatched to suboptimal kernels because the runtime lacks request-level hints about sequence length and token distribution.

Goal: Reduce prefill-side latency and tail by coordinating prompt preprocessing (tokenization + prefix handling) with kernel selection and the microbatcher. Deliver measurable p95/p99 reduction for interactive workloads (<= 512 context) while preserving throughput for long-context workloads. Target: 30-50% reduction in prefill median and 25-40% reduction in p95 for 0-512 token requests on benchmark suite A (interactive set).

Approach (high level):
1) Tokenizer lookahead sampling: run a cheap, vectorized UTF-8/byte-run sampler on the ingest thread to estimate token count range and character distribution (avg bytes/token, presence of unicode clusters). Emit a small hint object (3 bytes) that travels with the request as a kernel selection hint.
2) Kernel-aware prefetch queue: extend the microbatcher queue to accept hint-tagged requests and maintain separate queue lanes (low-latency lane for short/interactive, throughput lane for long). Each lane is associated with preferred kernel profiles.
3) Async prefill pipeline: move expensive steps (full tokenization, prefix dedup lookup, KV segment generation) off the critical path by performing an asynchronous precompute that can complete before the request is scheduled on GPU. If precompute completes early, attach precomputed KV/prefix to the request. Fall back to on-thread tokenization if precompute misses.
4) Prefix-segment bloom cache: introduce a fast probabilistic cache (bloom + LRU slab) keyed by short fingerprint of leading tokens to short-circuit duplicate prefix work for high-frequency shared prompts (e.g., system message templates).
5) Microprofile-driven kernel hints: before dispatch, runtime evaluates short histogram (from sampler) + model config to pick between latency-optimized kernel (low-batch, lower prefetch) and throughput-optimized kernel (larger batch, fused kernels).

Trade-offs and risks:
- Added complexity in request lifecycle and debugging (need good tracing and observability).
- Bloom false positives cause occasional unnecessary cache hits — must ensure correctness and safe fallback.
- Extra memory for async precompute queues; need caps and backpressure to avoid OOM under bursty traffic.
- Heuristics may need per-model tuning; start with conservative defaults and enable per-model tunables in model profile.

Acceptance criteria: [see acceptance_criteria field below].
acceptance_criteria: Instrumented traces that show the prefill-sampler hint attached to >=95% of requests in the interactive benchmark run.
Benchmark A (interactive, 0-512 tokens): end-to-end p95 reduced by >=25% and median reduced by >=30% compared to baseline runtime-1.22 on the same hardware profiles.
No functional regressions: outputs must match baseline tokenization/decoding for 100% of sampled test prompts (deterministic tests + fuzz suite).
Feature gated behind runtime flag and per-model profile switch; rollout plan documented and tested in staging with canary flows.
Resource caps prevent unlimited async precompute; under stress tests, system does not exceed 90% CPU and memory budget for prefill workers.
Design doc + operation runbook checked into Confluence and referenced from PR.

Postmortem/lessons doc if p95 not improved after rollout (owner: Diego/Aisha)
notes: 2026-02-28: Kickoff meeting. Consensus on hint approach and lane idea. Agreed on conservative defaults to avoid per-model regressions.
2026-03-03: Prototype sampler implemented; microbenchmark shows sampler adds ~200ns median overhead on ingest and produces a 3-bit token-length bucket with >92% accuracy on short prompts.

2026-03-05: Early end-to-end staging run (interactive set) shows 28% median prefill reduction and 22% p95 improvement when async precompute is allowed to complete before dispatch (hardware: g4dn-like cluster).
2026-03-08: Observability work in progress; need to add new traces: hint-generated, precompute-start/complete, cache-hit/miss, lane-assigned, kernel-picked.

2026-03-10: Discovered race on request cancellation path: if a request is cancelled while async precompute is in flight, KV prewarm can leak memory. Added cancellation hook and backpressure controls to worker pool (patch landed in runtime PR 2574).
2026-03-12: Integration with microbatcher lanes completed in feature branch. Next: run full benchmark suite A/B comparison across multiple instance types and model sizes.
Notes on rollback: the feature is behind a flag and a per-model opt-in; rollback steps documented in rollout task.
